subject: physics
question_text: A particle moves in a straight line with uniform acceleration. Its velocity at time t = 0 is v₁ and at time t = t is v₂. The average velocity of the particle in this time interval is (v₁ + v₂)/2. Is this statement true or false? Substantiate your answer.

verification.note: Unit 3 has NO Long Answer section in either source book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The Fastrack (pp.6-8) lists 4 Very Short Answer and 6 Short Answer questions plus a PROBLEMS section; the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.4-5) has a Short Answer section ONLY (5 questions) and no VSAQ section. The mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Motion in a Straight Line · 4 marks

steps.label: The verdict
lines: The statement is TRUE, but only because the
steps.why: With uniform acceleration the velocity changes at a steady rate, so the velocity spends as much time above the midpoint as below it. That symmetry is what makes the simple average correct.
common_mistakes: Answering "true" with no condition attached. The uniformity is the whole reason.

recall.must_convey: That the statement is true, and true because the acceleration is uniform.

steps.memory_tip: True — but only for UNIFORM acceleration. Say the condition.
steps.margin_note: Commit to true or false in the first line.

steps.label: The displacement
steps.why: Substituting a in terms of v₁, v₂ and t removes the acceleration from the expression, leaving the displacement written only in terms of the two velocities.
common_mistakes: Leaving a in the final expression, so the average velocity cannot be read off.

recall.must_convey: That substituting a equals v two minus v one over t into s equals v one t plus half a t squared gives s equal to v one plus v two over two, times t.
accept: v one t plus half a t squared
v one plus v two by two times t

steps.memory_tip: Replace a by (v₂ − v₁)/t. One t cancels and the average appears.
steps.margin_note: This is the two-mark step. Show the substitution in full.

steps.label: The average
steps.why: Dividing the displacement by t leaves exactly the arithmetic mean, which is the statement that had to be tested.
common_mistakes: Stopping at s and never dividing by t, which leaves the claim unproved.

recall.must_convey: That dividing by t gives the average velocity as v one plus v two over two, so the statement is true.
accept: v one plus v two by two

steps.memory_tip: Divide by t at the end. That last division IS the proof.
steps.margin_note: Close by answering the question that was asked.

insider_note: Both books ask this. The answer is TRUE, but only because the acceleration is uniform — say that condition or the proof is incomplete.
